descripcion_geo: City in the Ephraim Mountains, in the geographical heart of Canaan, about 35 km north of Jerusalem. Located in a sheltered valley between hills, it was the first permanent central sanctuary of Israel after the conquest. Identified with the current Khirbet Seilun, where excavations have confirmed Israelite occupation from the period of the judges.
clima: mountain Mediterranean; moderate rainfall in winter, dry and warm summers.
recursos: Olive trees and vineyards on the surrounding terraces
importancia_estrategica: First permanent seat of the Tabernacle and the Ark of the Covenant after the conquest of Canaan. Religious and administrative center of the twelve tribes during the entire period of the judges. Its destruction by the Philistines c. 1050 BC It marked the end of the tribal era and the beginning of the monarchy.

periodos.nombre: Israel Central Sanctuary — Period of the Judges

otros_habitantes.descripcion: Dominant tribe in whose territory Shiloh was located. Their tribal leadership was reinforced by the presence of the central sanctuary in their area.

otros_habitantes.nombre: Canaanites of the region of Ephraim
otros_habitantes.descripcion: Previous settlers of the hills of Ephraim who were not completely displaced during the Israelite settlement, according to the book of Judges.
Priestly family that administered the shrine of Shiloh for generations. His sons Hophni and Phinehas corrupted the cult, precipitating divine judgment on the house of Eli.

historias.titulo: The Tabernacle and the Ark of the Covenant at Shiloh
historias.descripcion: After the distribution of the conquered territory, Joshua installed the Tabernacle in Shiloh and from there distributed the portions of land by lot to the tribes that had not yet received an inheritance. Shiloh became the religious and legal center of the Israelite tribal confederacy for about 150 years. The Ark of the Covenant remained there until it was captured by the Philistines at the Battle of Eben-Ezer.

historias.titulo: The call of Samuel in the sanctuary of Shiloh
historias.descripcion: Hannah, wife of Elkanah, goes to Shiloh to the sanctuary every year and prays anguishedly for a son. Elí the priest, seeing her moving her lips without sound, mistakes her for a drunk. Ana explains her prayer and Elí blesses her. Samuel is born, who is consecrated to the Lord and left in Shiloh at the service of Eli. One night God calls Samuel three times; the boy finally responds after Eli's instruction. The first oracle of Samuel announces the judgment on the house of Eli.

historias.titulo: The destruction of Shiloh and the loss of the Ark
historias.descripcion: The Israelites take the Ark of the Covenant out of Shiloh to the battlefield against the Philistines in Eben-Ezer, trusting that its presence will ensure victory. But the Philistines defeat Israel and capture the Ark. Eli's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, die in combat. Upon hearing the news, old Eli falls from his seat and dies. Shiloh is destroyed and is no longer mentioned as an active sanctuary. The prophet Jeremiah will use Shiloh as a paradigm of divine punishment on the temple of Jerusalem centuries later.

personajes.descripcion: Israel priest and judge who administered the sanctuary of Shiloh for forty years. She received and raised the child Samuel. His inability to correct his sons Hophni and Phinehas, who abused the offerings and the women of the sanctuary, caused the oracle of condemnation of his house. He died upon learning of the capture of the Ark.

personajes.rol: Mother of Samuel — prototype of the prayer of petition
personajes.descripcion: Wife of Elkaná and mother of Samuel. His prayer in the sanctuary of Shiloh, said in silence under the weight of sterility and family humiliation, became a model of interior prayer for Jewish tradition. His song of thanksgiving after the birth of Samuel is considered the literary antecedent of the Magnificat.

personajes.rol: Israel Driver — installed the Tabernacle in Shiloh
personajes.descripcion: Successor of Moses who led the conquest of Canaan and chose Shiloh as the seat of the Tabernacle for the distribution of the conquered territory among the tribes. His decision made Shiloh the first permanent Israel sacral center in the promised land.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Shiloh was the Jerusalem of the Israelite pretemporal era: the place where the divine presence resided in the Ark and the Tabernacle during the tribal confederation. Its destruction was interpreted by the prophets as foreshadowing the fate of the Temple of Jerusalem if Israel abandoned the alliance. The memory of Shiloh functioned as a theological warning for centuries.

judaismo.fuente_secundaria: Talmud Bavli, Berakhot 31a-b — la oración de Ana como modelo de las dieciocho bendiciones (Amidá); se aprenden de ella seis leyes de la oración correcta
judaismo.descripcion: Hannah prays in Shiloh, moving her lips without making a sound, pouring out her soul before the Lord for her sterility. His silent and interior prayer became for the rabbis the definitive model of Jewish prayer.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Anna's prayer establishes that authentic communication with God is internal and direct, not necessarily mediated by the priest or the external liturgy. Their song anticipates the theology of divine reversal: the humiliated is exalted.
judaismo.posible_relacion_cultural: The song of Anna (1 Sam 2:1-10) is recognized by exegetes of both traditions as a literary model for Mary's Magnificat in the NT.

cristianismo.fuente_secundaria: Orígenes, Homilías sobre Lucas 7 — identifica explícitamente el cántico de Ana como prototipo del Magnificat de María
cristianismo.descripcion: Mary's Magnificat in Luke's gospel closely follows the structure and vocabulary of Anna's song. Both women celebrate the divine reversal of the social order: the humiliated is exalted, the powerful is brought down.
cristianismo.similitudes: Both songs celebrate the action of God that exalts the humble and brings down the powerful; Both women are mothers of figures who inaugurate a new era in the history of salvation.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: For Christian tradition, Anna prefigures Mary and Samuel prefigures John the Baptist. Shiloh as a place of consecration anticipates the temple as a place of presentation of Jesus.
cristianismo.posible_relacion_cultural: The Anna-Mary typology is one of the most studied narrative parallels between the OT and the NT in patristic exegesis.
